label: Squarish-shell 3BR / baths DISTRIBUTED, ROOM-AS-SPINE — no dedicated hall room at all; the full-depth great_room itself is the only circulation, and every bedroom doors directly onto it. Sourced from pep_SHD-2016026-DESIGN1. Zero corridor area cost, traded for every bedroom conceding rule 1's bedroom-off-public preference rather than just one tight-lot bedroom.

adjacencies.note: great_room + kitchen form the open LDK (gr style), matching the source's continuous LIVING/DINING/KITCHEN strip

master doors directly into the great_room, at its front end. FIXED from the source: pep_SHD-2016026-DESIGN1 routes the master's only door through an unlabelled nook at the south end of the KITCHEN with no other opening — an unsanctioned room-through-room pass-through, the single worst finding on that sheet. The source's own notes recommend exactly this fix: 'swing it off the front end of the LIVING instead of off the kitchen nook.' Fixed here at essentially no area cost, per established catalog practice of correcting sanitation/access issues found in source drawings.
master's ensuite — interior door off the bedroom
ensuite shares the kitchen's wall — matches the source's genuine shared plumbing wall between the two, both against the blind firewall side
br2 doors directly into the great_room's rear end, matching the source's BEDROOM2 opening straight onto the DINING strip with no circulation room between

br3 doors directly into the great_room's rear end, matching the source's BEDROOM1 (renamed br3 here to avoid clashing with the schema's single-master slot) opening onto the same rear widening of the strip

common bath doors directly into the great_room's rear end, matching the source's T&B opening onto the same rear lobby-widening as both standard bedrooms. NOT corrected to a buffered/hall-served door: doing so would add a hall room and contradict this topology's entire premise (the public LDK strip as the sole circulation spine, at zero added corridor area). Kept as a documented, deliberate rule 1 [PREFER] deviation — the source's own compliance notes make the same trade explicitly and this is the family's defining, novel feature (see catalog_mapping.novel_features on the source record).
the standard pair shares a party wall at the rear — matches the source's BEDROOM1/BEDROOM2 shared wall
geometry only, no door — matches the source's common T&B / BEDROOM1 shared wall

soft_proximities.note: keep the shared bath beside the standard pair, matching the source's rear-lobby clustering of both bedrooms and the bath

lot_adjustment_profiles.name: compact_sq_center_spine_baths_ds_gr
lot_adjustment_profiles.rationale: This parti has zero dedicated-hall area cost — the great_room itself is the spine — so it should out-compete every hall-bearing squarish sibling on compact lots and the profile triggers relatively late (95 m²). The source's own room widths (public strip a constant 3.5 m; bedrooms 2.9-4.3 m least dimension) suggest a natural floor in the mid-80s once caps bite; below that, the great_room's depth can no longer host three separate bedroom doors plus the bath door along its rear wall without doors colliding.

notes: Squarish 3BR catalog topology — ROOM-AS-SPINE, sourced from
pep_SHD-2016026-DESIGN1. Named center_spine for its position in the
grammar (the public LDK runs the full depth on the plan's centerline, the
same geometric role a corridor spine plays elsewhere in the catalog), but
unlike every other _spine or _hall member of the catalog, there is NO
dedicated hallway room here at all — the great_room doubles as both LDK
and the sole circulation route to every bedroom and the bath. Slug omits
the usual [_hall] segment for exactly this reason: it has none.
Layout intent (canonical, west = firewall side, left):
West column:  [master (front) : ensuite | kitchen (rear, wet-stacked)]
Center spine: [great_room — LDK + circulation, full depth, entry front]
East column:  [br2 : br3 (rear, party wall) : common (rear)]
This is a deliberate, fully-documented family member, not a cost-cutting
shortcut: every bedroom door and the bath door open onto the great_room
itself rather than a hallway, which is exactly the source's own defining,
novel feature (see pep_SHD-2016026-DESIGN1's catalog_mapping.novel_features:
'the public LDK strip is the sole circulation spine ... the catalog's parti
tokens all assume either a corridor or a two-column zone split; there is no
token for room-as-spine'). Rule 1 [PREFER] (bedrooms/baths off dedicated
circulation, not public) is broken by every private room in this topology,
not just one tight-lot exception — recorded here exactly as the source
record's own compliance notes recorded it, rather than smoothed over.
One correction WAS made, because it crossed from a documented [PREFER]
trade into an unsanctioned violation: the source's master bedroom door
opened through an unlabelled kitchen nook (room-through-room, not just
room-through-public). Re-routed here to door directly into the great_room
like its siblings — same [PREFER] concession as br2/br3/common, but no
longer a HARD-adjacent access fault. See the master<->great adjacency note.
Wet core: partially stacked, matching the source — service/kitchen/ensuite
share one plumbing run down the firewall side; common bath is isolated on
the opposite side with its own drop (traded for giving the common bath an
exterior window, per the source's own reasoning).
Firewall side: the source's west wall is fully blind (no openings for its
entire run) — worth preserving as siting guidance on party-wall lots, though
not separately encoded in this schema version.
Carport: NCP base form; the source shows a 3.0 x 5.4 m open carport on the
opposite (east, lanai) side from the firewall. Declare via brief.carport_side.
STATUS: NOT SHIPPED — recommend dropping. Investigated 2026-08-13, same
treatment as its two siblings from the 2026-08-12 drop. Topology unchanged;
these notes are the whole deliverable.
The authoring-time claim of 'a reproducible, environment-specific solver
issue' was WRONG and is removed. As authored this is the over-constrained-
anchors trap: left_anchored + right_anchored + zone_split declared together
are infeasible at every lot size. Bisected at 25x25.
The anchors are not the noise here — they ENCODE the parti. left_anchored
[master, ensuite, kitchen] and right_anchored [br2, br3, common] describe
exactly the three columns the label calls for, with the full-depth great_room
as the middle. Keeping them and dropping everything else was tried in all
four combinations (rear+stacks+zone, rear+zone, stacks+zone, rear+stacks) and
every one is INFEASIBLE. The only configuration that solves is dropping
left_anchored + right_anchored + zone_split — i.e. discarding the parti.
Two of the file's own declarations contradict its own label, which is worth
knowing if this is ever redrawn:
- zone_split is axis 'horizontal' with private_side 'rear', which puts the
public rooms in a FRONT BAND. That cannot coexist with a 'full-depth
great_room' spine, which is a vertical arrangement.
- kitchen is declared public by zone_split yet also appears in
rear_anchored, so it is required at the front and at the rear at once.
- front_to_rear_stacks puts great IN FRONT OF br2, br3 and common, again a
front-band reading, not a spine.
WHAT THE FEASIBLE VERSION ACTUALLY IS, and why it is not worth shipping.
Dropping the three gives a front block of great_room + master with every
other room in a rear band — bedrooms still door straight onto the great_room
(the hall-less idea does survive), but there is no spine and great_room is
not full depth. Measured at 13.5 / 14 / 15 / 16 square:
great       38.5  42.0  52.5  53.2   — 47-48% of the whole floor at EVERY size
br2 / br3    6.0   6.0   7.5   6.0   — at or beside the 6.0 m2 PD 1096 floor
Adding floor area never reaches the bedrooms; it goes to great_room and
master. Two of three bedrooms sit at the legal minimum at every size.
It is also a near-duplicate of 1s_3br_sq_front_back_split_baths_ds_hall_gr,
shipped 2026-08-13 — the same front-block-plus-rear-band shape, differing
only in having no corridor — and worse in every proportion (great 48% vs
39%, both bedrooms at the floor vs 6.0/7.5). It reaches no smaller lot
either: infeasible at 13x13, feasible 13.5-16, essentially the same band.
So it would add a second, weaker copy of a topology the catalog already has.
RECOMMENDATION: drop the file. The hall-less-3BR idea is already covered by
the shipped front_back_split sibling, and the center-spine idea deserves a
redraw from pep_SHD-2016026-DESIGN1 with a genuinely vertical spine, not a
patch of this graph. Kept for now only so the decision is yours.
